properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-05-29 to Chesapeake Appalachia Llc in Meshoppen Twp, Wyoming county. 78a81(a)2 - CASING AND CEMENTING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to prevent migration of gas or other fluids into sources of fresh groundwater.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Chesapeake Appalachia Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-12-20
Violation Code: 78a81(a)2 - CASING AND CEMENTING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to prevent migration of gas or other fluids into sources of fresh groundwater.
Violation ID: 886064
Permit API: 131-20590
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Meshoppen Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-05-29
Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr ¿Stepped¿ pressure build-up tests ¿SPBUT¿ being performed on all (5)wells on the HUNTER pad. The HUNTER 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H wells. These tests are being performed in response to a gas migration investigation in area underway by The Department. SPBUTs were initiated on 5/26/20 @ ~ 08:15 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - All (5) wells on the pad are shut in w/ Frac valves installed on top of well heads. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a temporary poly vent tank via rubber lines. All annuli were closed when I arrived. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Reps. Craig Shores and Trey Sites, Creston Consultant Reps., Tom Messing and Andy Sallaway and D.E.P. OGIS, Ken Kennedy. Starting at approx. 10:15, ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for all the HUNTER Pad wells. - HUNTER 5H: (20x13): 3.0 psi.; 68 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:17 ** (13x9): 277 psi.; 85 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:23 ** (9x5): 327 psi.; 85 % CH4; Sample collected at 10:27 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:20. - HUNTER 6H: (20x13): 17.0 psi.; 65 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:33 ** (13x9): 169.0 psi.; 87 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:37 ** (9x5): 549.0 psi.; 86 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:40 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:40. - HUNTER 22HC: (20x13): 24.0 psi.; 91 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:45 ** (13x9): 226.0 psi.; 89 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:49 ** (9x5): 396.0 psi.; 92 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:52 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:50. - HUNTER 21HC: (20x13): 44.0 psi.; 93 % CH4; Sampled collected @ 10:55 ** (13x9): 268.0 psi.; 90 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:00 ** (9x5): 131.0 psi.; 87 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:07 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 11:00. - HUNTER 23HC: (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0 % CH4; No sample collected (13x9): 255.0 psi.; 89 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:13 (9x5): 321.0 psi.; 86 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:20 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 11:30. - All (5) wells (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened and venting to poly tank @ 11:45. ** The presence of pressure and gas was detected in the (20x13) and the(13x9) annuli of all the wells on the pad with the exception of the HUNTER 23HC (20x13) annulus.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 924725
Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/27/2021
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of a release of an estimated 5 gallons of hydraulic fluid to the pad surface on Pad B. This inspection was only conducted on Pad B. I met with EQT Company Man Bill Mitchell upon arriving on location. He showed me the location of the release which was along the edge of the well site secondary containment in the travel lane near the company man trailer. The area had already been scraped and backfilled at the time of this inspection. The company man said that the release had occurred from a radiator on a cement truck that was offloading into the upright cement tanks at the time. The truck was straddling the edge of the well site secondary containment so the fluid leaked onto the pad surface. The cement trucks were moved onto the secondary containment as of this inspection. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected. The sump that is in place on the opposite side of the pad surface has had a metal lid placed on it. This sump was installed after fluid with elevated conductivity was discovered by the Department in that area of the pad. The electrical conductivity of the fluid in the sump was approximately 1350 uS/cm. The area around the sump on the pad surface was dry during this inspection. Violations remain outstanding in association with this release.

Continue to determine the cause of elevated conductance discovered during previous inspections to prevent future occurrences. Remove the elevated conductance fluids and contaminated soils from the pad surface and the sediment basin.2. Continuously monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered.I left the site at 1525 hours.

Comments: On 04/17/2025 the DEP conducted a routine inspection (IR #3960352) of Chesapeake Appalachia's (Expand's) Them Well Pad in Wysox Township, Bradford County. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) 1.8-3.45 mS/cm. The DEP collected samples. On 05/07/2025 the DEP received the sample results and cited violations (IR #3974712). On 10/08/2025 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection of Chesapeake Appalachia's (Expand's) THEM Well Pad in Wysox Township, Bradford County. The weather was 55 degrees and partly sunny. Rain fell on the pad within the last 24 hours. I arrived at 0915 hours.The site remains stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. There were two infiltration berms onsite. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) between 190.7-904 us/cm. There were four produced fluid tanks equipped with an internal secondary containment. There were six gas processing units (GPUs) onsite. There were ten temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment onsite. There were six wells capable of producing. They were each properly tagged with the American Petroleum Institute (API) identification numbers.This case has been referred to the Environmental cleanups and Brownfields program and all violations will remain outstanding until results have been reviewed and compared to Act 2 standards by the ECB program, and an approval letter has been issued.The following violations remain open against API #015-23911:35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)CSL 402(b)I departed at 1015 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BULL RUN RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/25/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 956913
Permit API: 083-56364
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Lafayette Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/25/2022
Comments: This well was stimulated on 5/17/2022 and is currently being produced with a pump jack. The operator information is displayed on the pump jack. The pit used during the completion of this well has been reclaimed. Earth disturbance associated with reclaiming this pit and installing gathering lines alongside the spur road to the location has not been temporarily stabilized. A film of oil is evident on numerous trees along the southern edge of the location (beyond the pit). Stained soil with elevated specific conductivity (SPC) is also evident along various pathways across the forest floor downslope of where the pit was located. This is indicative that during the notching and/or frac'ing of this well, fluids associated with doing so were not sufficiently directed and/or contained in a pit. Two valves on the frac tank located at the southwestern corner of the well site are currently open and brine/production fluids are actively dripping out of them. Crude oil is pooled at both ends of the tank near the discharge points (valves) and the soil is stained for several feet downslope of each. SPC readings of the soil near the discharge points exceeded the upper limits of my field meter (20,000 uS/cm). Trees near the west side of the tank appear stressed as a result of the discharge from the tank. These observations are indicative that an appreciable (unknown) amount of brine/production fluids were released through the open valves on this tank. I contacted Justin Hansen of Bull Run and scheduled a field meeting to review these findings and discuss remediation options.

Comments: On April 14, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The area where the water was seeping out near the northwest stormwater vault observed on March 3, 2022 was not flowing. The hole in the well pad trench liner near the northwest stormwater vault has been fixed. Two patches have been added to the trench liner. The soil in the area where the water from the seep had been pooling up has been excavated and removed. A small berm has been built in the area and a tarp has been dug in to collect stormwater. This area is being vacuumed as necessary. The DEP screened the pooled water on the downgradient side of the built berm and the conductivity was 365 uS/cm. An area to the south of the area impacted from the seep of the northwest stormwater vault that had been previously excavated to remove contaminated soil from the seep was screened for soil conductivity. The screening resulted in a measurement of 2.42 mS/cm in a small area. The area of high conductivity was shown to STL Resources Ken Shade. There was about 8 inches of water in northwest stormwater vault. About 12 inches of water was in the southwest stormwater vault. The water was not high enough in either vault to be measured for conductivity due to not being able to reach the water levels with the field water quality meter. There has been no pad surface remediation completed. The DEP screened the five seeps and three stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 20.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 21.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 26.4. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 190 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 274 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 32.6 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 40.1 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 169.4 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 23.8 uS/cm. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers. Infiltration berm 1 along the access road that had a section erode observed on February 18, 2022 has been filled in and compost filter sock has been added near the berm. The other four infiltration berms with erosion noted in Inspection Report 3324293 have been filled in. The infiltration berms along the access road have not been seeded or temporarily stabilized. It appears that earth work on the infiltration berms along the access road has been completed. The DEP recommend seeding and temporarily stabilizing the infiltration berms according to ¿102.22(b). This will help with preventing another situation of sediment discharging outside of the LOD and help prevent accelerated erosion of bare earth. Infiltration berms 1, 2, 6, 7, and 9 appear to be holding water and not infiltrating within 72 hours. The DEP recommend investigating into the functionality of these berms to avoid over topping or berm erosion. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation ID: 8267341
Permit API: 051-21425
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: German Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/10/2026
Comments: On March 10 2026, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the CFR/USX 5 OG Well in regards to OGI referral.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department traveled down the access road towards the well site. Approximately halfway down the access road, the Department observed water flowing onto the access road. The water was observed continuing to flow down the access road where it appeared to end at the well site. Erosion channels appear to have formed along the access road as a result of the flowing water.Upon further inspection, the water appears to be originating from a drainage channel/tributary to Antram Run. It appears that a culvert located under the access road may be damaged or obstructed, causing the water to flow onto the access road rather than through the culvert. The Department was unable to locate/inspect the culvert inlet. However, no water was observed discharging from the culvert outlet. Based on these observations, it appears the water is flowing from the drainage channel/trib to Antram Run onto the access road rather than through the culvert.Upon further inspection of the well site, the well appeared equipped for production. A well tag was present on the well head, however had a previous operator listed (Apex Energy). No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface of the wellhead.A well posting was observed on a piece of production equipment and appeared to have all required information. However, it appeared damage and almost falling off. A production tank was observed onsite and appeared in sound condition. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface around the production tank.Prior to leaving the site the Department spoke with operator representative Heather Empfield and informed her of the E and S issues related to the access road caused by the flowing water as well as recommended a new well tag/well posting be installed at the well site.Ms. Empfield stated that she would contact the site foreman to inform them of the Department's observations and they would work to assess the site and correct any issues as necessary.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed erosion of the access road, failure to maintain the culvert, as well as failure to have the well properly posted.

Comments The Department (Jon Sassi-DEP, EPS) received a phone call from Mike Demming (Senior Regulator Analyst-SWN) on 2/7/17 at 1601 hours to self report a release of less than 5 gallons of diesel fuel. The release was discovered at 1405 hours. Mr. Demming explained that a US Well Services heater trailer (line heater which keeps water from freezing during hydraulic fracturing operations and has since been taken to their yard for repair) was exiting the location and was tilting forward on the access road when the diesel fuel overflowed the belly pan and was released to the access road. The diesel fuel traveled along the access road being carried by stormwater (raining at the time of the release) downslope and flowing into the roadside ditch along Hawk Road. The belly pan is used to collect leaks and overflow from the heater trailer. The operator failed to clean the belly pan prior to demobilization. A mini excavator will be used to remove any impacted material and a vac truck will remove and impacted fluid. SWN will conduct PID screening after excavation. He stated that the visibly impacted material will be taken to the Tunnel landfill via the Meshoppen Rail-yard. The Department (Jon Sassi and I) arrived on site to conduct an Incident Inspection in response to Mr. Demming's report. At the time of the inspection Consolidated Well Services was drilling out frac plugs. We met with Justin Johnson (Construction Supervisor-John Miller) at the time of the inspection. Mike Demming later arrived on site and both gentlemen joined us during our inspection. We walked along the access road and moved stone around in areas that appeared to have residual sheen. We followed the residual sheen upslope to an area on the access road that appeared to be the point of impact. Mr. Demming field screened the areas and got readings between 0.7-112 PPM on his PID. Ed Blystone (Well Site Supervisor) met with us during the screening. We then walked down the access road where Mr. Demming explained that an approximate 1 quart of diesel fuel was recovered by the vac truck at the Hawk Road roadside ditch. They also removed stone and some material beneath the stone. When we inspected the area, the ditch was already reworked and new stone was in place. During this inspection, it was found that sheen was still present. There are 2 sandtraps and 2 heaters attched to the flow lines for each of the 3 Marcellus wells. Mularz expects Flowback will move off site in about 3 weeks.Chesapeake spudded surface holes on April 13, 2023 for 3 new Marcellus wells at this site. They finished drilling the 3 wells into the Marcellus in June 2023. Records show there is also 1 well spudded here in May 2012 and plugged in March 2013. Universal hydraulically fractured the 3 Marcellus wells on July 10-24, 2023. Deep Well Services then used a workover rig with rig assist snubbing unit to drill out plugs in the 3 wells August 1-5, 2023. Environmental Oilfield Solutions regraded the gravel pad surface during a previous inspection on August 16, 2023. properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Repsol Oil & Gas Usa Llc

Violation Date: 2019-04-25
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 848032
Permit API: 015-23420
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Columbia Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-04-25
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of Repsol's Monro G (03-142) Well Pad in Columbia Twp, Bradford County on 4/25/2019 at 0830 hours. The weather was sunny and 50 degrees. The inspection was conducted in response to a notice to the department that on 4/25/2019, during the 2nd stage of the 3H well, a piece of iron washed out and released a mixture of frack fluid and sand to containment. The washout created a "jetstream" of fluid with a reported ~9000 PSI of pressure behind it. This stream of fluid cut through the secondary containment liner, the primary containment liner, and dug through some pad material. An estimated 15 gallons of frack fluid and sand mixture was released through the hole. A vac truck was onsite to recover sand/fluid mixture from containment. Most of the fluid was recovered. The vac truck was also used to suck fluid that had collected in the hole through containment. While I was onsite, crew was flowing back and flushing the well to be able to shut it down. After shutting the well down, we were able to assess the impacted area. Golder was onsite screening the area off the northern edge of the pad. No evidence of impact was reported and I didn't observe any impacts off containment besides the hole that was created. The area of the containment that was breached was just east of the 5H wellhead. The hole was approximately 1 foot wide. Golder screened the soil as far into the void as possible. Their highest recorded reading from the impacted soil was 2.53ms/cm. No standing liquid was visible downhole. Small amounts of fluid remained on the containment and I obtained a reading of 17-18ms/cm from one of them (see photo #6). Kris Perritt agreed that this fluid would be representable to the fluid out of containment. Kris plans to have the iron, rig mats, and containment pulled back to learn the extent of the void to fill it in for safety purposes. Upon soil screening of the area, impacted soils would be excavated and disposed of. Golder planned on taking soil samples from beneath the containment and the sampling results would be forwarded to the DEP. Due to findings throughout the course of this inspection, violations of the following are cited against well API #015-23420: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a) 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 35 P.S. 6018.301

Comments: I received a text message on April 3rd 2023 from the OGI that was checking on the flaring operation being conducted on the Hill Lease in Brokenstraw twp Warren county operated by Universal Resource Holdings. He said there was a oil spill that appears to have taken place awhile ago coming from a well close to the one being flared. On 04/04/2023, I followed up on the information, Brad Hofert from Universal resource holding was onsite at the time of my inspection. Brad said a valve had frozen and blew out on the number 21 well over winter. The valve was replaced and absorbent pads were used to clean up around the wellhead. I returned to the site on 04/05/2023 to gather photos and take another look at the extent of the spill.Evidence of the crude made it down slope approx 150 feet but stayed inside the tire ruts. More than likely carried by snow melt and rain. Oil soaked leaves and some oxidized crude can be seen in the tire ruts. The estimated release amount is around 5 gallons of crude. I spoke with Brad about getting the oil soaked leaf litter cleaned up and some of the soil next to the well head removed. He agreed and said he would get a crew together and a mini excavator to scrape up the area near the well head. With the estimated volume of this release and the small affected area, this is a non reportable release. The oil covered leaf litter and impacted soil will need to be properly disposed of.

The location consists of one very large well location and a separate tank pad. The location is overgrown and clearly has not been tended to in any way for some time. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/13/2022 to EQT CHAP LLC in Sewickley Twp, Westmoreland county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT CHAP LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/13/2022
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 972774
Permit API: 129-29003
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Sewickley Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/13/2022
Comments: On October 13, 2022, the Department conducted a Routine inspection at the Sinay well pad in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself, ET Marcella Dantzler, those listed from the SWDO OG Team, and EQT representatives Joe Eversman and Logan Dominick.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was at the entrance of the access road, and was not obstructed by vegetation (see photo 2). The ER and PPC plans were not available immediately upon arrival (see photo 3). A site safety and environmental plan was found in the office onsite. A PPC plan was also in the office, but missing required components. Neither the secondary containment inspection records nor the well permit were available onsite when requested. A sediment basin was observed along the left side of the access road, looking towards the pad. A forebay cleanout was observed on the opposite side, with a culvert connecting them under the access road (see photo 5). Cattails were observed in the sediment basin. A further review will be conducted to ensure that they are part of the PCSM plan. A soil stockpile was observed along the left side of the access road, immediately before entering the pad (see photo 6). The operator was actively drilling onsite. This is the first well being drilled. The operator intends to drill 4 wells total. A destabilized area of soil was discovered behind the sound wall on the eastern side of the well pad (see photo 15). Preexisting metal and brick was observed outside of the LOD at this location, as was noted in the site E and S plans (see photo 16). A tear in the rig site containment was observed at the southern side of the pad. This was brought to Mr. Eversman's attention, who immediately called in a crew to repair it (see photo 12). Tanks and containers onsite that contained regulated substances were labelled, showed no evidence of leaks/discharges (see photos 13 and 14). The production tanks were within secondary containment (see photo 17). A puddle was observed at the northeastern corner of the containment. A soil conductivity reading was taken in this puddle, which read 200 Micro Siemens. The rig site containment appeared to be nearly full at its northeastern corner. A soil conductivity reading was taken at this corner, which read 390 Micro Siemens. The Department inquired with Mr. Eversman about whether the containment is pumped regularly. Mr. Eversman stated that the site containment gets pumped multiple times daily as needed. A pump truck later came to pump the containment during this inspection. A sediment-laden discharge to WOTC was discovered upon returning to the access road entrance (see photo 23). This discharge was flowing into a sewer drain that emptied into a field across the road from the well pad, through a culvert (see photo 21). This culvert was found to be approximately 80% full with sediment (see photo 22). Near the end of the inspection, EQT representative Logan Dominick arrived to the site, who was informed of the Department's findings. Mr. Dominick was able to provide an electronic copy of the PPC plan onsite, this was requested to be emailed to the Department for further review. He also stated to the Department that CFS and a silt pad will be installed around and over the sewer grate to prevent further discharge to the WOTC. He also stated that the site ERP and PPC plans had previously been placed into the mailboxes attached to the Act 9 sign, and that they were likely removed by a nuisance third party.Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that the aforementioned unstable soil spot behind the sound wall is re-stabilized. Violations are being issued for discharging to the waters of the commonwealth, failing to have an adequate ER AND PPC plan onsite, failing to have the drill permit onsite, and failing to have secondary containment inspection records onsite.

Comments: On 07/24/2024 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Southwestern's (SWN's) Vanorder-Patrick (12 Pad) Well Pad in Herrick Township, Bradford County. The weather was 70 degrees and cloudy. Rain fell on the pad within the last24 hours. I arrived at 1035 hours. The site remains stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. There are two post-construction stormwater management structures onsite. They appear to be functioning properly. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 192.8-262 us/cm. There was no evidence of any spills or releases. There was one produced fluid tank held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine gas processing units (GPUs) held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine wells capable of producing. There were each properly tagged with the American Petroleum Institute (API) identification numbers. There were numerous temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment onsite. Violations remain outstanding at this site from a previous release. Site remediation has been performed and a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEPs Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed.The DEP recommends:1. Disposing of stormwater held in the secondary containment structures as soon as possible to maintain compliance with 25 PA 78a64a(e).I departed at 1135 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/07/2024
Violation Code: 78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well.
Violation ID: 8186067
Permit API: 065-26775
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Knox Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/07/2024
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#302235). This well is located approximately 1,444' from the complainants water well. The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, and possible failures. The well is equipped for production and is currently producing. The well is equipped with a required check valve. Well records, production reports, and mechanical integrity assessment reports were reviewed to assist in the investigation and are current. As part of the investigation 4 slam bar holes were placed into the ground in the cardinal directions approximately 6" to 1' from the well-head and approximately 3' deep to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. A Bascom-Turner Gas Explorer II gas meter which was calibrated on 05/06/2024 was used to take the soil gas readings. A soil gas reading of 4% LEL on the North slam bar hole, 32% LEL on the East, 2% LEL on South, and 10% LEL on West was observed at the time of inspection. As a result of the soil gas readings around this well the following violations are being cited: Violation: 78.73(b) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to prevent gas, oil, brine, completion and servicing fluids, and any other fluids or materials from below the casing seat from entering fresh groundwater, and prevent pollution or diminution of fresh groundwater. Violation: 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING - DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. Violation: 78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well. Violation: 78.73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected. At this time, the Department is requesting that the operator conduct an investigation to determine the source of methane around the well.
